venues.name: Miel Bakery
venues.description: Cosy, classic French bakery offering housemade breads, pastries & seasonal tarts, plus hot drinks.

reviews.text: I wanted to love this bakery but I felt my almond croissant was a little too sweet. It was well filled and the pastry was extra buttery. The cinnamon buns looked amazing here so I would come back to try. Only two outdoor seats for seating. Pastries range from £3.5-£6 so some are definitely on the premium priced side. My almond croissant was £4.50.

As we were eating our croissants outside an older lady walked past and blared out “I can’t just walk past, I have to get one”. And it makes sense once you try one. Delicious heavenly croissants. This is an exceptional bakery offering a range of both sweet and savory croissants.
A truly lovely local bakery with amazing pastries. Out of the oven fresh, all absolutely delicious made with fresh and quality ingredients. Their coffee is also phenomenal.

The worker made our experience greater than expected! Friendly and helpful worker. We loved the Flat White and Iced Hojicha. Nice and quiet place (we were there around 3-4pm). Overall experience is 5/5 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟! Will definitely come back.

Amazing bakery. My favourite in London! All the classic French pastries are delicious! Don’t miss their pain au chocolat, kouign amann, banana bread and the daily special square croissants. The coffee is also great :)

venues.name: TOAD Bakery
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
The line is long but it moves relatively
quickly! The pastries are delicious and fresh - get the kalamansi and coconut iced bun, this was cheap but delicious, cornbread croissant was savoury but could’ve done with more jalepeno, plum danish was ok, and the everything bagel croissant was delicious! Tastes just like a bagel, but in croissant form so it’s super buttery and flakey.

The least favourite was the Jaffa cake, texture was a bit too dense.

Would queue again!

This was a very nice pastry, and to be honest they seemed to have tonnes of great options. It was delicious! My only gripe with this place is that the queue was mental - I was in it for 45 minutes. I have no issue with a place being popular but the queue was barely moving which was slightly frustrating.

The line was sooooo long and you look at it, and think is it worth it for a bakery??

And let me tell you… it is SO worth it. I truly believe this is the best bakery in London and is worth every single person in line waiting for pastries. We ordered so much and enjoyed every last bite. They had a collab at the time and we had a beef curry pastry which was fab. The pastry just tasted incredible, the different savoury and sweet options were an added bonus.
Great place. Sometimes you need to wait for quite a while but its worth the wait. Lovely pastries, lots to choose from: both sweet and savoury. Go there!!

Legitimately my favourite bakery in London because of their friendly, neighbourhood welcome, their interesting experimenting with bakery products and of course everything is excellent. I can highly recommend their sandwiches as well as the cakes on offer!

venues.name: GAIL's Bakery Soho
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Amazing food. We had baked eggs with streaky bacon with toast soldiers. It was so good. No lactose free milk though. Oat or soy only.

What an excellent little cafe. The drinks and pastries are fantastic and the service is very warm and friendly. The cafe in itself is small but cosy and I will certainly be purchasing from other branches too.

I went out of my way to visit as id seen some good reviews.
They were a bit limited and what they did have wasn't exciting me in terms of cake.
I did get what looked like a cinnamon bun in a mushroom shape and with chocolate in.
It was dry . Barely any chocolate.
It was a disappointment.
Some of the savoury food looked lovely.
No steps to get in.
Some seating available.
Near Oxford street.
I don't think I'd try again
Quaint spot. Amazing baked good! And delicious porridge. Comfort food on an autumn morning. 💖

The service is amazing. We liked the hospitality.
The manager (Anass) is very friendly with customers and professional.

venues.name: Brother Marcus Borough
venues.description: Contemporary cuisine that's as Instagram-worthy as it is palate-pleasing. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: Came a few weeks back for an anniversary dinner. Absolutely outstanding food and service, thoroughly looked after. We sat outside and it's perfect for a cool evening in the late summer. Drinks menu was extensive and we'll definitely be back. Also thought it was incredible value for money we were totally stuffed for £50pp and had 2 drinks each.

After walking one round in Borough with not many places to sit for a meal, we headed towards Brother Marcus that is also pet friendly.

Alfresco dining was beautiful and the food is delicately made. They use very fresh ingredients and you get a taste of Mediterranean.

The pita and hummus dip was a delight to begin the meal with the pan fried bream and prawn pasta.  The pasta was well
Made. Maybe even hand made.

We had two lovely desserts

Amazing food and service. This is my second visit to Brother Marcus. The chicken was cooked to perfection, moist, flavourful and not dry. The fluffy pita bread is incredible. It was a summer evening so everyone sat outside and it was a vibe. The service was great and they know the food menu well. Phil who served our table was a super star, polite, caring and attentive. I will come back.

Shah's an amazing server! Very attentive and explained the menu in great detail. My friend had  a few food allergies and the staff went above and beyond to accommodate.

The food was delicious and I can't wait to come back! The best dinner I've had in a long while 😊

If you’re wandering through Borough Market and need a place to park yourself with good food and good vibes, this spot has you covered. The atmosphere is effortlessly chill — the kind of place where time slows down and you forget you only “popped in for a quick bite.” Pro tip: book ahead unless you enjoy the thrill of disappointment.
Here’s the twist: the vegetables here totally upstage the meat. The broccoli and aubergine skewers? Stars of the show. Order them or regret it later. The halloumi with honey is a dreamy little number for those who like their savoury with a side of sweet. As for the calamari… it’s fine, but no standing ovations. We also ordered chicken but I didn’t find it special.

Flavour-wise, they deliver. Price-wise… well, your wallet might raise an eyebrow. Still, if you want a market-side feast where veggies take the crown, this is your spot.

venues.name: Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

attributions: Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone
Sunday in Brooklyn - Modern American Restaurant Marylebone

reviews.text:
I finally got to try the famous Sunday in Brooklyn pancakes, and they were absolutely lovely. Perfectly fluffy, rich in flavour, and not overly sweet, just the right balance that makes them so easy to enjoy. I can completely see why they’re so popular.

On top of the food, the service was excellent. Our server, Marcus, was incredibly attentive and made sure everything was just right throughout the meal. His thoughtful service really added to the experience.

All in all, it was a fantastic visit, and I’ll definitely be coming back again soon!

Well… I came 3 times to this brunch spot to try different dishes.
Breakfast egg sandwich 10/10. Fluffy and well cooked eggs and a spongy bun!
Steak&eggs 9/10 both egg and steak were good and perfectly cooked but the potatoes on the side were a bit dry and tasted like left over potatoes.
Their famous pancakes 10000/10000 really yummy!

Great spot for breakfast! The vibe is really nice and the place is pretty big with lots of seating. Overall, the food was tasty, but I tried their signature pancakes ‘Sunday Pancakes - single' (which is quite big for me and my friend) and felt they were a bit too sweet for me 😅 not really my thing

We enjoyed our meal here today, especially the Shakshuka and Cauliflower Melt burger. The portions are large, with great presentation and rich American flavours.

Staff were friendly and welcoming. We enjoyed the ambience but it was a bit loud in some parts of the restaurant. It was packed with people, and is extremely popular so we’d recommend booking a table in advance, especially on weekends. If you can, ask for a table where it’s quieter.

Overall, great value for money and highly recommended for an authentic American meal.

One of my favorite breakfast spots in London — I always make sure to visit! First time trying this branch though, and the vibe wasn’t as nice as Notting Hill. Food was amazing as always (the pancakes are a must!), but service was a bit unorganized and we had to remind them about our order. Still, I’ll definitely come back! 💛

venues.name: Eggbreak
venues.description: Hip cafe focused on egg dishes, from omelets to eggy pastas, in casual digs with juices and liquor.

reviews.text: We had to download an app in order to book a table. The menu had a great selection of egg dishes, all very tasty and different. It also had sweet dishes and salads. The food was tasty and flavours were great but it is quite pricey for eggs. Service was great. The atmosphere was nothing special.

I stopped by Eggbreak around 9:30 AM without a reservation and was pleasantly surprised to be seated after just a short 10-minute wait, not bad at all for such a popular spot.

The place itself is lovely. The interior has a warm, inviting charm that instantly makes you feel relaxed, and the atmosphere strikes a perfect balance between buzzing and cozy. What stood out just as much was the team, genuinely friendly, always smiling, and attentive without being overbearing. That kind of service goes a long way.

Food and drinks came out quickly, which was impressive given how busy it was. I was tempted to order the whole menu (seriously, everything looked amazing), but I went with the Turkish eggs, and they were absolutely excellent. Rich, flavorful, and satisfying enough to carry me through the day.

All in all, Eggbreak delivered on every level, great vibe, kind service, and food that truly hits the spot. I’ll definitely be back, and maybe next time, I will try everything on the menu

One of my favorite meals and best breakfast while visiting London! Portions were filling, juices were so good and the staff was busy but kind- would definitely come back here for breakfast! Inside is very cute and cozy as well

Small cafe (watch your head of you're tall!) with great food options for breakfast and brunch. The coffee is also really nice (free refills on the house brew). They also offer gluten free bread that was toasted to perfection.
There will likely be a cue when you arrive but it's worth the wait.

Eggbreak had been on my list since I moved to London a year ago. It’s a very popular spot, especially with tourists in the Notting Hill area, so I went in with high expectations. Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing.

Food:
I tried the Egg, Bacon & Cheese Toastie, it looked great but tasted very average, nothing special.

I also ordered Ari’s Pancakes, but couldn’t finish them as the bananas were not fresh, which was off-putting.

I ordered a pot of tea as well, but the tea strainer provided was clearly not clean (as shown in my photos), which was another let-down.

Service & Atmosphere:
The place was very busy, and while that reflects its popularity, the staff seemed rushed and a bit erratic. Service felt inattentive overall.

Overall:
Given all the hype, I expected much better food and service. There are far better breakfast places in London, and I don’t think I’ll be returning to Eggbreak. It would also be hard for me to recommend it to others.

venues.vicinity: SOUTH KENSINGTON STATION ARCADE, 1-3 Pelham St, London

reviews.text: Great dinner experience. Everything we ordered was delicious, and special thanks to our server, Raina! She was super helpful and kindly answered all my questions about the dishes and ingredients and made our dinner extra special:)

Brother Marcus is an absolute gem in London! The atmosphere is warm and stylish, with a relaxed vibe that’s perfect for brunch or a casual dinner. The food was outstanding — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The menu had a great variety of Mediterranean-inspired dishes, and everything we tried was delicious.

The service was friendly and attentive without being overbearing, and the staff made us feel right at home.
Can't wait to come back!

Had an amazing brunch at Brother Marcus on south Kensington ! The food was outstanding.

the fried chicken rösti with eggs was perfectly seasoned and beautifully cooked, the granola with apricot was fresh and light, and the scrambled eggs on toast were spot on. Drinks were refreshing too, especially the watermelon & pomegranate juice.

Service was friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was bright, modern, and welcoming. Everything was well-prepared, delicious, and nicely presented. A great spot for a relaxed brunch.

I’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend!
We had a great time here. The breakfast was delicious and the banana bread is a must-have. Our waitresses Jessica and Raina were super friendly. We would definitely come back again.

Brother Marcus is a lovely, quaint restaurant around the corner from South Kensington Station. As a family we were celebrating a milestone, and greatly appreciated the team's efforts to make us feel special with a bottle of bubbly and dessert. Special shout out to all the staff, the manager and Belle for creating a warm atmosphere coupled with wholesome, good quality plates of food. Would definitely recommend others to try this place!

venues.name: Duck & Waffle
venues.description: British & European cuisine 24/7 in a modern 40th-floor space that has floor-to-ceiling windows.

reviews.text:
Great food and service!  Maitre’d was very kind and accommodated our schedule change with grace and service.

Wonderful food, service, ambiance was scenic.

English breakfast was amazing, duck and waffles signature dish is like butter melting in your mouth.

An absolute amazing experience! Took myself on a solo date there and had a great time. The food was delicious, the service was impeccable. The waffle was light and fluffy and the sweet sauce complemented the duck just perfectly.  Strongly recommend!

I had a lovely experience at Waffle and Duck. The food was really tasty and beautifully presented, and the staff were very friendly and attentive, making us feel well looked after. Our order arrived quickly, which was a nice surprise. They also have a great selection of wines to complement the meal. On top of all that, the view is absolutely amazing – it really adds to the whole dining experience. Highly recommended!

We dined at Duck & Waffle as a group of 9, and everything from start to finish was absolutely exceptional. The food was delicious, the ambiance was vibrant yet classy, and the drinks were perfectly crafted. The service was also fantastic — attentive, friendly, and efficient, even with our large group.

Of course, the duck dish is a must-try — it absolutely lives up to the hype!

Highly recommend visiting Duck & Waffle when in London. It’s a memorable experience in every way — food, views, and vibes all on point!

We had a great time at our visit to Duck & Waffle. You can't beat the ambiance or views of the city (from the 40th floor!), the service was on point, and everything we ordered—from cocktails to food—was fabulous.

Recommended:
- Waffle on the Rocks
- Crushed Piña
- Spicy Verde
- CHEESY POLENTA CROQUETAS (insanely good)
- DUCK BARBACOA TACOS (also insanely good)
- CRISPY BBQ BEEF PUFFS
- CAESAR SALAD
- SIRLOIN AU POIVRE
- MAC ‘N’ CHEESE (lovely)
- TRUFFLE MASH (so good)

I will absolutely be back on my next trip to London!

venues.name: Milk Beach Soho
venues.description: Where contemporary London meets European flair - think Michelin-starred techniques with a side of British charm. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
We had an incredible experience at Milk Beach Soho for my friend’s birthday lunch. I called ahead due to train delays, and Kimberly kindly reassured me they would hold our table, a huge relief on such a special day.
From start to finish, everything was perfect. The ambience is relaxed yet vibrant, even the restrooms are beautifully designed, with calming ocean sounds. The food was delicious, thoughtfully presented, and portions were just right. We didn’t even finish everything, which surprised us!
A heartfelt thank you to Swiz, who truly made our experience exceptional. She was warm, attentive, and explained the menu with care, suggesting drinks tailored to our preferences and they were exactly what we loved. Her service struck the perfect balance of professionalism and friendliness without ever rushing us.
The birthday surprise was the cherry on top: a small dessert brought out with a lit candle, a handwritten “Happy Birthday” card, and a tiny gift box tied with a bow containing a bite-sized sweet. My friend described it as “a little piece of heaven.” That thoughtful gesture made her day.
It was our first time at Milk Beach Soho and certainly won’t be the last. Absolutely memorable in every way.

We visited Milk Beach in SoHo and had such a wonderful experience. The atmosphere was welcoming and stylish, and from the moment we arrived the service was friendly, attentive, and professional. The food was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every dish we tried felt thoughtfully prepared and exceeded our expectations.

Overall, Milk Beach is a fantastic spot that combines great service with outstanding food. We’ll definitely be back and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting SoHo.

An absolutely amazing experience. From the moment we arrived, the service stood out - the host who checked our reservation was warm and welcoming, and our waitress was lovely throughout.

We sat out on the patio, which truly gave off beach day vibes - the atmosphere felt like a little summer escape in the middle of Soho. We were a group of six, and everything was handled smoothly and efficiently.

We tried a good number of cocktails (all fantastic), and honestly worked our way through most of the menu ; which, while not huge, is well-curated. The portions were generous, the food was excellent, and the setting just elevated the whole afternoon.
Highly recommend for a relaxed, sun-soaked outing with great food, drinks, and service.

I recently went to the barre and yoga socials at Milk Beach and it was such a fun experience! The classes were super well run – Brittney did an amazing job organising everything and bringing in great instructors who made the sessions both challenging and enjoyable. After the workouts, everyone hung out over share plates and cocktails, which was the perfect way to relax and connect with others. On top of that, there were lots of goodies given out just for attending, which was such a nice surprise. Overall, such a well put together event – can’t wait for the next one!

An absolute gem! The food was delicious, the prices are incredibly reasonable and the venue is great. But what really sets this place apart is the staff - they went above and beyond to accommodate all our needs (thanks Kimberly!), we’re wonderfully attentive, and genuinely lovely. I wish I could give them 10 stars! Definitely becoming a regular here.

venues.name: The Breakfast Club Soho
venues.description: English and American breakfasts, plus comfort foods and burgers in cheerful, quirky surrounds.

reviews.text: Cozy breakfast spot located right in the heart of Soho serving delicious savory dishes. An absolute refreshing change from the usual sweet heavy brunch menus. We visited as a group of six and were seated impressively quickly, which is rare for central London. The staff were warm, attentive and made us feel welcome right away. I was especially impressed by their Strawberry Matcha. High quality, vibrant and just sweet enough. The Iced Latte with an extra shot of caramel was also excellent. As for food, I recommend the Smashed Avocado Toast topped with crispy bacon, and hash browns. Generous portions and packed with flavor. If you’re after a savory brunch spot with great service, central location and fair pricing, this place is well worth a visit.🥑🍳

Overall a good experience, the staff were really friendly but the service was a little slow. We pre booked but were only allowed the table for 1 hour, so it felt a little rushed because we were celebrating a birthday. The food itself was really good but I would really recommend pre-booking as there was a long queue if you hadn't. For vegans there is a lot of choice.

This place is great. We waited around 15 minutes for a table but understandably so. It’s so good. Well worth the wait. I went with my mum and she got scrambled eggs on an absolute door stop piece of sourdough. Both were cooked to perfection. I got the Big Stack and my god it was good. It had the best of both worlds: pancakes and bacon/egg etc etc. so full I didn’t finish it. Also had a delish vanilla matcha.
They have a few locations in the city so if the one you want to go to has a queue then there will be another not too far away!

Perfect place for a good breakfast in Central London! The All American is pretty good, the poached eggs in particular were cooked properly. I did not like the pancakes, they were too thick in my opinion. In any case, I would recommend this place.
Consider a relatively quick queue for entering.

Restaurant specializing in breakfast. The menu goes from a full English to fluffy pancakes and every breakfast item in between. There's a short cocktail menu if you need that morning mimosa. The service is friendly, swift and helpful. The restaurant is card payment only.
Ordered the Eggs Benedict, my go to dining out breakfast item. The eggs were overcooked. The muffins were tough, spent a lot of time sawing through them.
Overall it was tasty but not a pleasure to eat. I told the staff this after they asked and was offered a free coffee.
Was disappointed with the quality of what I ordered, but would go back and order something different.

venues.name: The Table Café
venues.description: Breakfast-to-dinner British fare served in a bright, modern space.

reviews.text:
We were really impressed by The Table! It’s a small, charming restaurant with a very cozy atmosphere and lots of plants that give it a lovely, rustic touch. The menus are colorful and nicely designed, and the staff were all super friendly and attentive.

We had The Table Full English — a classic English breakfast and everything was absolutely delicious and served hot. The quality of the food was excellent, and you could really taste that it was freshly prepared.

They also offer vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options, which is fantastic. Debora was especially knowledgeable and gave me great advice on the gluten-free alternatives available.

A big thank you to Debora, who took such great care of us and gave wonderful service and recommendations. :)

We can definitely recommend this place — great food, warm atmosphere, and lovely people!

We visited The Table again today, and once more we were absolutely delighted. The dishes were freshly prepared in the open kitchen, which we really love — it’s such a great and inviting concept.

This time, we had the brunch classics: Smoked Ham Hock + Chorizo Hash with Halloumi and an Avocado + Feta Toast with bacon. Everything was delicious and beautifully presented.

Our server today was Daniel, who double-checked my gluten-free option and made sure everything was just right. He provided excellent service.

Very much enjoyed my meal out on Saturday, sheltering from the rain.
Waffles (with cinnamon pear and shortbread crumb) were gorgeous and they were happy to accept my substitutions. So many options, I was overwhelmed! Will just have to come back 😁😁
Our server was so nice and really made the experience extra special.

The food at The Table Café is amazing! We ordered a burrata salad and a classic English breakfast, and everything was absolutely perfect.

We had to sit outside because there weren't any seats inside, which wasn't our favorite thing, but honestly, the food was just so good that it made up for it!

Beautiful cafe with a lovely secluded outdoor seating area. Outdoor seating is under large canopies with heaters. Indoor seating is lovely and open with an open kitchen at the back. Service was fantastic, we waited only a couple of minutes for a table. Food was really good. We had the eggs royale and brunch waffles. Both were brilliant, really tasty and decent size portions. The ice chai latte was also so good, like a milkshake! Seems to be popular so would recommend booking if you really want to come.

venues.name: The Breakfast Club Seven Dials
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
\\ A Singaporean Girl Review 🇸🇬

What makes this place special?

I’ll give you three reasons.
1️⃣Generous servings of GOOD food.
2️⃣Excellent roasted beans for coffee.
3️⃣Great atmosphere and mood.

We came all the way from King’s Cross Station. There is also another outlet there but this outlet has a higher review point and we understand why. Throughout our meal, there was a queue outside. The half & half was generous! And the flat white was delicious 😋

Shoutout to the lady at the door (Analgar), she knew her stuff and the product offerings. Though the menu was generically written as beans, she could advise us not to take shashuka for those medically allergic to fava beans 🫘 as it was a core ingredient. She also reminded us again upon serving- what a conscientious gesture.

Highly recommended. Only thing to improve would be the door, that kinds of slams hard. Otherwise, all good.

Fantastic breakfast place although we made the mistake of not booking a table as it was very busy! Ended up waiting for 5-10 mins to be seated.

Otherwise the food was absolutely delightful – easily one of the best breakfast venues we’ve been to. Beautiful fluffy waffles, superb full English and great coffee.

Service was very good too, quick, friendly and professional. Well done to the Breakfast Club!

Expensive, but serves good quality food and is insanely popular (mostly with tourists). Expect to pay around 16 quid for each dish, and just over 3 quid for a small mug of tea. There are probably better (and cheaper) breakfasts to be found in London, but the large variety on the menu means there's something here for everyone, and the staff are extremely helpful. I will definitely be going back if I stay in the area again.

The food is amazing and they really take care and the time to learn about your allergies and explain what they can offer as an alternative. The staff is some of the friendliest I have encountered in London. They serve with care and joy! Even though it’s really busy and you have to wait up to 30 minutes sometimes to be seated, It’s a really cozy and relaxed vibe from the moment you enter

Our first experience with a English breakfast restaurant. The wait was kinda long as was a very popular spot. Gave us time to talk to the locals outside and every Briton we met was nice and helpful. Finally got in and got amazing service. Went with the English breakfast and it was good. Not my cup of tea but sure it's fantastic. Glad we stopped by!

venues.description: Modern European dining that doesn't take itself too seriously, but takes your taste buds very seriously indeed. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text:
Can definitely agree with all the great reviews.
Nice relaxing set up, although restaurant was full on a Sunday lunch time, we did not feel rushed and was served by a very pleasan Soniya.
Soniya carefully explained ehich are the Gluten free options and gave good recommendations.
Food is very tasty for wach of our dishes.
We had the Gluten free Fried chicken, Shasuka with oita and Soniya has kindly offered and extra piece of super fresh Pita on the house.
The Peach and Olive oil cake was divine. Its been a while I had good Gluten free cake.
Highly recommend this place .
Thanks Siniya for making this dining experience so pleasant.

Great brunch spot in a fantastic location!
Probably the best location you could ask for. The service is quite good — if they’re busy, you can leave your phone number, have a little wander, and they’ll call you when your table is ready, which is a brilliant idea. On the other hand, it sometimes feels like there aren’t quite enough staff inside; we were forgotten once and ended up paying at the bar after waiting a while for someone to bring the card machine.
Marcus tea looks lovely and tastes great if you’re a fan of chamomile, and the smoothies are excellent. Portion sizes are fairly standard. The Eggs Benedict wasn’t bad, though the mustardy flavour isn’t typical and not really to my taste — but that’s just a matter of preference. The shakshuka, however, was very nice.

Amazing food, so well seasoned and prepared. Mezza options with a tonne of options; the haloumi in particular is a must. The service was also excellent with the staff who were friendly, joyful and approachable, which elevated our time there.
Ayanthi was our primary waiter and she was delightful and made our experience even better!

Had a wonderful experience at Brother Marcus Covent Garden! The staff were super friendly and welcoming, and the service was excellent. A special thanks to AYANTHI  for her amazing service and warm hospitality. She made the visit even more enjoyable with great recommendations. The peach olive cake was something truly unique and left such an interesting and delightful taste in my mouth definitely worth trying! Highly recommend this place for anyone looking for good food and great vibes.

A really lovely restaurant. The food is delicious and the staff were all super friendly.
I knocked it down a star because of a few details.
We received one dish a long time before the others. It was a side dish, not a starter, so I'm not sure why this came out so early. Luckily it wasn't hot.
Also, towards the end of our meal, the staff became very inattentive. They cleared away our plates, asked if we wanted the dessert menu, we said yes, but didn't receive a menu for over 15 minutes. We had to ask a second time.
Their card reader didn't work, so they asked us to scan a QR code to pay instead. We both would have preferred to pay by the machine, so this was a little disappointing.
Overall, it was lovely and I'd definitely recommend, but I think there's some fine tuning on timings that could improve the overall experience.

venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: This is a great place for a cocktail. They have a wide selection of really fun ones. Beautiful bar and vibrant atmosphere. The only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars was the snack selection was pretty poor. We opted for the “House crisp selection” at £4.75, which turned out to be a tiny bowl of regular crisps with a sour cream dip on the side!

Me and my friend went there for a short hangout during the afternoon. There wasn’t any wait around 3pm.  If you are finding a bar with a bit of uniqueness, good vibes and of course with some good pictures, this is the place. The interior is really unique and well thought out, it felt really welcoming as well.

I had an mocktail and my friend had a rum cocktail, both drinks taste really good. I would like to try more next time!!! Just a note you will have to ask for mocktail since they aren’t on the menu.

Taking local advice to explore Soho for a fun night out turned out to be the best decision—and The Little Scarlet Door completely lived up to the hype! We stumbled upon this place while searching for lively bars in the area and were lucky enough to be offered a table around 10 PM without a reservation—a win in itself.

From the moment we walked in, the vibe was fun, quirky, and full of energy. The theme of the bar is super creative, and the atmosphere was electric with great music and even better cocktails.

A huge shoutout to Cass, our server, who was absolutely phenomenal—genuinely friendly, attentive, and made our visit that much more memorable. He really embodied the welcoming spirit of the entire staff.

We loved it so much that we actually came back the next evening after checking out a few other spots in Soho that didn’t quite measure up. Not only did the staff remember us, but we were lucky enough to have Cass serve us again, which made us feel like regulars.

Final Thoughts

If you’re looking for a fun, vibrant bar with excellent service, creative cocktails, and an unforgettable atmosphere, look no further than The Little Scarlet Door. This spot is officially on our list of must-visit places in London—and we can’t wait to return!

I’m only writing this for our star girl Erin!! She served us tonight for my best friends small graduation celebration. She was just the loveliest server and attentive. I never felt like I was having to catch her attention- she just knew when to come along and ask if we needed anything. 10/10 service and interior and drinks were exceptional. I will be returning and trying the rest of the other branches.

Thank you Erin again for making our little evening special even though we forgot it was actually a graduation celebration lol!!

Come here if you’re in Soho ✨ - George and Peter looked after us super well at the bar, even whilst it was busy!

We had some great shots and now our most favourite drinks - Never Been Kissed and An Affair to Remember. I’ve been to fantastic bars and tried incredible cocktails but Peter made the “An Affair to Remember” for me and it’s the best cocktail I’ve had in my life.
Trust me, try it, my friend is a gin fan and I’m a dark spirits fan but she loved it… it’s so balanced and smooth 😍

We went impromptu around 10pm - Great vibe in there, places to sit upstairs and downstairs but also space to dance which I love! The shower cubicle is such a chic touch.

P.S. Shoutout to the sweet man at the cloakroom for picking up my mirror - we love chivalry.

venues.name: Amazing Grace London Bridge
venues.description: Where innovation meets tradition - expect the unexpected in every beautifully plated creation. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

address.formatted: C Q G International Ltd, 9a St Thomas St, London

venues.vicinity: C Q G International Ltd, 9a St Thomas St, London

reviews.text:
A Night to Remember at Amazing Grace, London Bridge

Tucked away near the heart of London Bridge, Amazing Grace is unlike any restaurant or bar we’ve visited before. Housed in a breathtaking Grade II-listed 19th-century church, the venue effortlessly blends historic charm with vibrant modern energy. Think stained glass windows and original stone architecture meeting thumping disco beats and soulful live performances, it’s a unique sensory experience that grabs your attention the moment you step through the doors.

We visited on a Friday night, when the vibe was electric. The night’s soundtrack was built around disco, funk, soul, old-school hip-hop, and even some Garage classics, which were performed live with impressive vocals that got everyone moving. As we soaked in the lively atmosphere, we couldn’t help but admire how perfectly the lighting and acoustics complemented the stunning church setting; it's truly a party in a place you’d least expect.

The food was as memorable as the music. We kicked things off with the Amazing Grace Sharer, a generous and flavour-packed platter featuring crispy Japanese Fried Chicken, sticky-sweet Korean Chicken Wings, smoky Padron Peppers, juicy Corn Ribs, and moreish Korean Potato Bites. Each bite offered something bold, spicy, or savoury, a masterclass in Asian-inspired comfort food.

We followed this with a couple of Fried Chicken Baos, which were soft, fluffy, and bursting with flavour thanks to the tangy pickles, creamy Gochujang mayo, sesame, and spring onions. But the standout dish for us was the Chicken Burger. A free-range chicken coated in crunchy panko and sesame, layered with Kewpie mayo, fresh lettuce, and pickles. It’s rich, crispy, juicy, and a definite must-try. On the side, I ordered the Amazing Rice, which lived up to its name: a fragrant mix of spring onion and ginger oil, tare sauce, crispy onion, and sesame. It’s the kind of side you could happily eat on its own.

For dessert, we shared the Salted Caramel Brownie, served warm and delicately dusted with icing sugar. It was rich, gooey, and exactly the indulgent finale you want after a night of dancing and feasting. We also had a trio of Japanese Mochi Ice Cream—Mango, Chocolate, and Vanilla—which added a refreshing, chewy, and cool contrast to the brownie.

All chicken served here is halal, which made our meal worry-free and even more enjoyable. The mocktails were just as thoughtfully crafted as everything else. My wife had the Espresso Martini (alcohol-free), made with Amazing Grace’s house coffee mix and vanilla syrup; she called it one of the best she’s ever had. I loved my Grenadine Bramble, a bright, citrusy blend of Lyre’s Original, lime juice, sugar, and grenadine . It was refreshing, not overly sweet, and paired well with the food.

A special mention goes to Dio, who looked after us throughout the evening. Friendly, attentive, and genuinely warm, he made us feel right at home, even in a venue buzzing with energy.

By the end of the night, we’d not only eaten incredibly well, but we’d danced, laughed, and soaked up one of the most unique dining experiences in London. If you’re looking for a place that hits all the right notes, food, vibes, and service , Amazing Grace London Bridge is the one. We can’t wait to return.

Feel like this place has so much potential… The food was good and the music was entertaining, however found the staff rude. I could understand if the restaurant was extremely busy and staff were under pressure, however it wasn’t. Food is ordered from the bar and when I went to order, the staff member wasn’t friendly and it seemed a chore for them to take my order. I feel like the atmosphere was let down by the customer service. Overall, I don’t think I would return unfortunately

We went through using first table and the food was delicious! Atmosphere were great and the staff were 10/10, I lost something in there and the staff went above and beyond to help me find it. They also had a live performer ANDD a photo booth! Nothing to fault

I was out for First Fridays at the Tate Modern this month and a friend suggested we grab a drink at Amazing Grace afterwards. I wasn't totally sure what to expect, and while the walk over felt a bit longer than I anticipated, it ended up being so worth it.

There was a modest £5 cover, which honestly felt like a steal once we got inside. The energy in the room was electric! The live performers were phenomenal—seriously, the kind of voices that make you stop mid-sentence just to soak it all in. The upstairs lounge had a great vibe, and the dancefloor was already buzzing... and it was only around 10:15pm!

I spotted a few people still enjoying food, but unfortunately the kitchen had just closed by the time we arrived. Not a huge deal—just means I’ll definitely be back to give the menu a proper try. Between the music, the drinks, and the atmosphere, Amazing Grace has officially earned a spot on my regular date night list.

If you’re in the area and looking for something fun, lively, and a little unexpected—this place is it.

Fun night with tasty food and great drinks. Early evening visit was perfect before it got a bit hectic but sure it’s buzzing as the night goes on! The Korean Potato Bites were the absolute stars. So yum.

venues.description: A sophisticated escape from the ordinary, where every dish tells a story of culinary craftsmanship. Located in the heart of London, this is where London's food scene comes alive.

reviews.text: I definitely recommend this rooftop. It has a very modern and beautiful interior. Drinks are good and The alcohol is strong. Staff are extremely welcoming, friendly and kind. Our waiter recommended us what to drink based on our preferred flavours. One of our drinks came with a mini ice cream!

Not only the food choices are limited, the view is also limited compared to other roof bars in the world. There is only one corner of the outdoor area that can see St. Paul, the majority of the outdoor areas you are just facing ugly buildings. Food wise is so so, except for the potatoes with octopus which is quite good. Cocktails wise was a bit too sweet for our taste and just so so in general, although the presentation looks good. Service was friendly but slow. Price wise is quite pricey for its quality. Music was also so so in this place.

I had a blast in Florattica! My best friends have surprised me with a birthday brunch. Roberto, the manager was ever so kind to help us with our belongings. He welcomed us with a glass of bubbly and a big smile. The staff was ever so kind, we had fantastic waiters who served delicious food and bartenders were serving top-notch cocktails! The atmosphere in Florattica is amazing, you get that Dolce Vita vibes! I’m definitely coming back! - Well I did 😉 and got welcomed with a delicious glass of champagne 🥂🍾

Big thank you to Roberto, Michael, Juan and the lovely waitress from Nepal, you have made the end of my birthday weekend more memorable with your hospitality! 🎊🥰

Lovely seating area. Staff were polite and helpful. Drinks on the other hand were quite disappointing. Looked very different in real life compared to the menu, which I understand is meant to look artistic however it is also quite misleading. Shown photos below as an example. My boyfriend described them as tasting like acid reflux. If you favour good drinks over atmosphere I wouldn’t recommend going here.

The place is beautiful and have amazing drinks. Kabita helped us to choose the best drink according our taste and she 100% nailed it! The food was also VERY good! I was there for my husband birthday and they were above and beyond on making his day even better. We definitely recommend it.

reviews.text: A large, basement bar in Central London, right next to Covent Garden. I went there on a Saturday evening, all the tables were booked, but they let us in as there was still plenty of space around the bar. I had 2 cocktails, reasonably priced. There was live music, which added to the vibes of the place.

Loved the vibe here!! Great music, nice crowd, and an aesthetic atmosphere. The cocktails were solid, and the staff were lovely. Perfect spot for a fun night without it feeling too hectic! Definitely recommend going during the live performances regardless of the event🫶🏻

Truly an unforgettable experience. We’re here to have a meal before the theatre and what an absolutely treat and hidden gem. The space itself is dimlit and beautifully curated, the music not too loud so you can have a nice conversation without screaming at each other.

Then the food, wow what a surprise, I’d recommend the salmon fish and the tacos 🥹🥹 10/10!!

There’s happy hour until 8.30pm so that’s always a plus.

The best bit though would be the chef coming out and speaking with us - we felt so honoured for that. So thanks to chef James!

The service was also 10/10!

Anywho, would highly recommend, we’ll definitely be back!!

We came for Dinner. And the staff were amzingly attentive and so funny and fun.
We managed to even have interaction with the chef James. Such amazing food and would recommend coming here. We will be back especially as there is a live band and DJ's later. Thank you so much for the hospitality the whole team

Only had one drink but it is absolutely extortionate. Drinks are far too expensive for what they are - too much ice and barely any actual liquid. Took two sips to drink the cocktail and was left a bit underwhelmed. The bar itself has wonderful decor but the lighting was so dark and turned down you couldn’t even see anything else. Came on a Thursday so I didn’t expect it to be so busy but was more of a nightclub than a bar. Also was advertised bands would be playing and nobody was on. Just a DJ playing some average club songs.

However, I would like to come back on a Saturday when an event is on and hopefully try the food and see what the vibe is like from there on.

venues.name: Disrepute - Cocktail Bar in Soho
venues.description: Trendy, dimly lit basement bar with an old-timey feel & leather booths serving creative cocktails.

reviews.text:
Had an amazing night at Disrepute! Mateo gave us the warmest welcome, Jake was a fantastic host, and Lua and David absolutely crushed it behind the bar. The cocktails were next level — we tried the whole drink menu (designed & illustrated by GiGi) and we loved every single drink. Great vibes, incredible staff, and some of the best cocktails in London. Can’t wait to come back! 🍸
The playlist is also great 🎶

Go here! The service, team, drinks, ambience, and overall vibes are always on point. The new menu is a fantastic and fun adventure, and the classics are always perfectly balanced.

This bar is great because you step outside of the chaos in London for a brief moment into a place where you can relax and have great conversations, drinks, with nice music in the background. One of my favourite cozy speakeasy’s in London that does it right.

Luca and Aidan are always making phenomenal drinks, Jake, Lio, and Acene are always providing wonderful service, with Lua and David ensuring everything runs smoothly throughout the night.

Absolutely go here if you have the chance!

Personal favourite drink on the new Menu: Domination (don’t forget to open the scroll on the bow!)
One of the best cocktail places I've been. The mixologists know flavour and balance. Great service. Will be back. Could do with making some of the stools taller though 😄

Was fortunate to stumble upon this amazing speakeasy after my birthday dinner and I have to say, the cocktails were one of the best I've ever had I London. Bar was also not overcrowded which was a huge plus! Loved the bar snacks too, especially the crispy corn.

Not cheap bur with this level of excellence, you get what you pay for. I’d argue the best cocktail menu on Earth, the most attentive staff, and a high-end ambiance rare anywhere. Could not recommend it more. Support your local artisans.

reviews.text:
We had a fantastic time at Pulse Bar for our recent work event! From the moment we arrived, the service was top-notch – super friendly and attentive, which really set the tone for the night. The owner is amazing – warm, welcoming, and clearly passionate about making sure everyone has a great experience.
We had a blast playing beer pong, shuffleboard, and darts – such a fun setup that really brought the us together. The atmosphere was lively without being overwhelming, and it’s clear that a lot of thought has gone into creating a space where people can relax and enjoy themselves.
The drinks menu is extensive and genuinely impressive, with something for everyone – from cocktails to craft beers. The food was also spot on – tasty, well-presented, and ideal for sharing during a social night like this.
All in all, Pulse Bar ticked every box. The service, food, games, and overall vibe were exactly what we were looking for, and we’ll definitely be coming back. A brilliant venue for team events or just a fun night out!

I really enjoy coming to this bar when I go out, the drinks and the food is very nice. I love playing darts. My husband and my son enjoy playing pool. It's fairly priced, we went during happy hours so it was cheap. The staff is so lovely, they are welcoming and friendly. The place is kept clean and the atmosphere is great. They show football on the screens. I really recommend this place

Had one of the best sandwiches of my life with the best atmosphere. The bar was inviting and the owner was awesome. On top of that they had one of the sweetest dogs I have ever met. If I lived in London I would go all the time. Perfect for dinner or a night out on the town. The bar has some of the nicest beer pong tables I have ever seen. They are custom made with led lighting. Thanks to them for such an inviting experience.

Had an amazing night at Pulse Bar London Bridge! Michelle was an incredible bartender, friendly and made great drinks. Nico, the owner, was super welcoming. And the best part? Meeting Hermes, the adorable bar dog! Great vibes all around , can’t wait to go back.

Go for the owner’s crazy Italian energy and stay for the food, drinks and games. Pulse bar is designed for groups of friends to hang out and get competitive - beer pong, darts, pool and more. The burgers are delicious and beers are cold. Nothing fancy - just right. Make a date.

reviews.text:
The TOMATO - possibly the best cocktail I’ve ever had. Starts savoury in the mouth- like the scent of a really crisp cherry tomato. Then it transitions thru the sweetness of a cherry tomato and ends in raspberry. Still an earthier fruit so follows the tomato well but goes from savoury sweet beautifully.
Cocktail bar is inspired by Indian flavours, sweet and savoury, done so well. Curry flavours with spirits, Indian salad flavours done in a light cocktail ect. Also rec the Cucucumber and Nimbu!! Super friendly and chatty staff too

Arrived just after 6 PM about a 15 minute wait to get in. Well worth the wait, the cocktails were fantastic and the bartender is definitely put pride into their work. The Kokum was the pride of the show. Most unique, slight pepper, but delicious all around.

This super cool speakeasy bar, located in the heart of London, offers an incredible cocktail experience. The attention to detail in crafting each drink is remarkable, and the design is equally impressive. While it may be a bit pricey, the experience is definitely worth it. If you’re a cocktail enthusiast, this place is a must-visit!

Love the Indian inspired cocktails with the hip hop music vibes!  Like I was truly impressed and happy I got a chance to visit on my recent trip to London!  The creativity of the menu and the vibes at Somo were first class!  It’s a must visit on any trip to London.
One of the best cocktail bars I’ve been to in London. Very reasonably priced and well-made with great strength. Amazing service and atmosphere.

venues.vicinity: Sea Containers House, 20 Upper Ground, London

reviews.text: A incredibly beautiful cocktail bar with beautiful drinks crafted with an immersive storyline. Whilst a bit pricy, the service is impeccable and the overall experience is worth it for a nice treat. I tried the Baloo-Za and Cosmo Salad, both were wonderful with a fruity taste. I also tried the Vantapink Gimlink, rather strong but a must try in my opinion. There is a special menu for vegans, I would recommend the blistered peppers and aubergine dip as they pair wonderfully with the drinks.

Wow, amazing cocktail creations and a lovely view of river Thames. The cocktail creations are described in detail in the menu, which helps to find something matching your taste and preferences.
Beside the cocktails the food is excellent! Try the tacos - some of the most amazing tacos I ever had in my life!

Some of the best cocktails available in London. Set on Sea Containers. Beautiful hotel. Really innovative choices, not seen anywhere else. Using unusual unique muxes, cornflake infusion did instance. Excellent DJ and right by the Thames. Well worth a visit

First time visiting…. LOVED It! The service was impeccable! The devote music and atmosphere was chilled and sophisticated.
Had snacks… well presented and tasty!
Seating was comfortable and had a great view on the the Thames.
Champagne ( we had 3 bottles) was crisp and cool.
Will definitely visit again!

Service was amazing, particularly Lockie. The drinks are perfect for a particular type of person. Initially what I got was very light and delicate. Not to my tastes but it did say it was light on the menu. They then didn't have the ingredients for the main drink I wanted to try (it happens) so I got what they listed as their second heaviest cocktail. It was incredibly sweet and I couldn't taste most of the ingredients.

This bar is great for a particular type of person, but if that's not you then you're out of luck. If you want very light and delicate cocktails with absolutely no alcohol taste, you'll really enjoy this place, but it just wasn't for me personally.

address.formatted: Roof B, Bussey Building, 133 Rye Ln, London

venues.vicinity: Roof B, Bussey Building, 133 Rye Ln, London

reviews.text:
After failing to get into another nearby rooftop bar, we ended up at Bussey Rooftop instead. It’s on the 5th floor of the building, but getting up there was a bit of a mission. The lift is this old industrial type that felt a bit sketchy, and you need a code to access the top floor, otherwise it only stops at the 4th. If the weather’s not too hot, I’d actually recommend just taking the stairs. There aren’t many stairs in between floors, and it’s probably quicker.

Once up there, the space itself is okay but a bit underwhelming. The menu is super limited, with only a handful of drink options. Ordering is easy with a QR code at the table, though.

The biggest letdown was the atmosphere. The whole place smelled a bit like rubbish and it was so warm and muggy. We came up hoping for a bit of a breeze and fresh air, but the space is mostly walled in and there are no fans, so it just traps the heat.

Definitely not the rooftop escape we were hoping for.
Great views, music and decor! Cocktails weren’t amazing but there were a range of spirits. Would probably return if in the area.

Can't go wrong with in made Pizzas and great beer selections. Roof top views and great temperature with easybup and down windows. Great, happy team and a DJ spinning some great beats!
Great for groups or nice intimate time too.
Hopefully the lift is working otherwise the stairs are a great way to earn that first beer!

Great selection of Alcohol free options available too.
SO gorgeous! Such a lovely vibe and great music. We went after the outdoor cinema which is right next door

Had a the most incredible private party at Bussey Rooftop Bar. The events team were so attentive in the build up, making sure every detail was covered and the bar team on the day could not have been more friendly and made the whole event run effortlessly smoothly. The views and set up inside are just magical, such a great place for a party! Thanks to Nick, Sasha-Sky, Colin and the rest of the team!

reviews.text:
Been here for drinks a couple times after work and on the weekends. The drinks are GOODDDD 10/10. Recommend a pina colada, it banged differently! All the cocktails look really nice.

The service was slightly slow when I last went, and we took the service charge off. The staff didn’t really seem too bothered about taking it off which made it seem a bit weird. It wasn’t busy and it took 15/20 mins for 4 drinks to come. Only disappointing thing about this place to be honest.

Also, sometimes they serve the drinks in glass and then other times they serve it in plastic cups!!!

Views are amazing! Worth a trip if you love cocktails and really want to some stunning views of the city.

Amazing views and decent prices. We visited on a Monday evening, so it wasn't crowded. The waiter was really helpful and had a good knowledge of wines. The fact that it wasn't busy made our visit really relaxing. Would definitely recommend.

We had a fantastic time starting our day with vermouth and cocktails followed by the chef’s incredible menu. Denise was absolutely fantastic in explaining (bit of a complicated) menu. The vibe is amazing and I must also praise the music list. Overall worth every penny!

The food was fine. Steak was tasty, some main dishes were the size of the brunch portions, though we were told they were main course size. Champagne 🍾 was flowin,  and cocktails 🍸 were perfect. We could not dine in the sun but overall it was a pleasant experience and we would returned knowing the food menu better. Staff was were attentive and friendly.
Roof top bar with a fantastic view. Very accommodating  servers. You can see The Shard and see Tower Bridge from the roof top. It was a lovely evening.

venues.description: Vibrant open-air bar on a rooftop terrace offering an extensive drinks menu & light fare.

reviews.text: Great vibe, food was amazing. Tried to extend our 2 hour booking but sadly were told no. Would come back next time we’re in London. A great time was had.

We got served by Alex who was awesome and then another Alex came and sang happy birthday to my friend which was also awesome and unexpected. This is the place to be if you are in London bridge. Excellent beer and wine selection. Amazing atmosphere and super nice staff..

It was okay, the atmosphere is what made the experience for me. It was busy and the music was good. Waiting times were good, I went around 6-7pm. The stairs weren’t that bad on the way up to the rooftop; but I can imagine it would be a lot harder coming down when you’re drunk. I liked the food, but this place isn’t something that you come to eat if you get me. The staff were friendly but as a small con; the seating area wasn’t good where I sat, it was quite cramped. Overall I would say 3.5

I was amazed when I was shown upstairs to my table…The panoramic view of London is unreal as well as the venue itself.The staff are super friendly and accommodating to your needs,I had Bebe show me to my table she was so lovely and made sure I had everything I needed. The drinks were perfect they were just as good as they looked,as well as the food being tasty and quick service so it was still hot.Overall my experience was 10/10 I will definitely be coming back with friends very soon :)
Lovely place to be and enjoy , good vibes , good service , lovely cocktails , 🍹 lovey staff , only thing your have to climb the mountain which is good 👍. I loved my time here , highly recommend

venues.description: Chic rooftop venue for creative local eats & drinks, plus views of The Shard & St. Paul's Cathedral.

reviews.text:
The food & service was brilliant. We came for my mum’s 60th birthday lunch and the whole experience was perfect.
Great views and a quiet atmosphere (we came on a Thursday)
We thoroughly enjoyed the food and the cocktails were also great!

Beautiful quiet and off the busy roads restaurant-cum-hotel. Close to station. The restaurant is on the rooftop terrace and offers sitting inside or outside.
While it's beautiful, there's something missing to add to the magic of a rooftop dining experience.
The service and staff were good but it doesn't quite hit the 5 star.

Mercer roof top terrace boasts a fantastic location with stunning views over St. Paul’s Cathedral. The atmosphere is chic yet relaxed, perfect for any occasion. Service was impeccable—attentive and friendly throughout. The food was a highlight: beautifully presented surf and turf, absolutely delicious desserts.Highly recommended!

Without a reservation, luckily, on a Monday, we managed to get a table. We ordered drinks, and mine came wrong, so they had to redo it. Then the main courses were served. Although delicious (beautiful flavours), my friend found a hair in her food, so it was replaced. I ordered lamb, and halfway through, I found a hair! The waitress was very embarrassed and apologetic. They removed the lamb from the bill and offered a complimentary drink for her risotto. A nice gesture, but the evening was quite spoilt by the overall experience.
Loved the ambiance of this place, perfect for summer vibes. The food was surprisingly nice. I will come back again.

venues.description: Views over the city are on offer from this modern 10th floor restaurant filled with live plants.

address.formatted: above Assembly Hotel, Alhambra House, 31 Charing Cross Rd, London

venues.vicinity: above Assembly Hotel, Alhambra House, 31 Charing Cross Rd, London

reviews.text: This is a very fun restaurant! Great views of the city! The food was fine you’re mainly paying for the great views. All the workers were very friendly. It definitely can get pretty busy so you might want to book ahead.

We came for a Bottomless Brunch beforehand a theatre matinee. The menu is fixed price and it's clear before you arrive whats included so do take a look at the menu before booking to be sure it's right for you. We had  3 x soft tacos, rice and a dessert. All were great and quite filling. To drink, it was as much Prosecco and frozen margarita's as you fancy in the 2 hours.  The atmosphere is fun and loud. The views are great given it's a rooftop restaurant. Would recommend if you are looking for somewhere fun with friends especially if it's not all about the food and more about having a good time.

I had a really nice time here celebrating my friend’s graduation. First time experiencing a rooftop restaurant and was impressed. This was a nice intimate spot

We ordered a few large plates, though our chicken and potato dish wasn’t enough to share between 7 people. Food was lovely and flavourful.

Had a really lovely young waitress who served us.

£55 for bottomless sugary margaritas (with 0 alcohol in them) uncooked rice and burnt chocolate sauce....

Not happy.

I had 10 or 12 frozen margaritas, the waitress made sure she kept them coming. Even with minimal alcohol I would've been atleast a bit tipsy. Instead I had a lot of sugar. There's also a.prosecco option but that has sulphites and gives me a migraine.

The tacos were okay. Nothing to scream about.
The rice that accompanied them was undercooked and crunchy. You could cut it with your nail and see the white line in each grain. Rice isn't hard to get right.

And for dessert, the churros were nice and chewy but the sauce??? When you burn chocolate it almost tastes sour. I tried to salvage it by mixing the white chocolate with it but no. Just had the churros.

The view is nice but wouldn't come again.

Absolutely loved it!
I had an amazing experience at this rooftop Miradora restaurant. The atmosphere was vibrant and full of energy — perfect for a fun evening out.

The view over London was absolutely breathtaking, especially at sunset – definitely one of the highlights.

But what truly made the night special was the bar – the cocktails were outstanding! Every drink was beautifully crafted and full of flavour.

Huge compliments to the bartender Alex – not only were the cocktails delicious, but he was also incredibly friendly, professional and clearly passionate about his craft.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for great vibes, amazing views, and unforgettable drinks! 🌇🍸🌮

venues.name: Aviary
venues.description: Elevated seasonal dishes served in a stylish rooftop restaurant that has sweeping city views.

address.formatted: Royal London House, 22-25 Finsbury Square, London

venues.vicinity: Royal London House, 22-25 Finsbury Square, London

reviews.text: We came here on a Saturday evening and can say im surprised this place doesnt have solid 5 stars. Absolutely lovely place. The venue is very nice, decor is stylish but subtle. Views are amazing outside too. Staff were all very friendly and service was great. But the food, that was the best part. Really impressed with the flavours of both the mains we had, lamb and the pork. Even the side dishes were amazing! Fries and the potatoes. Eton mess was nice although the chocolate dessert was nicer I think. Cocktails were great flavour too. Obviously price is higher than some places here but id say its worth it considering the quality.

The Aviary proved to be a great place to meet up with old school friends for Sunday lunch - this place is quite the little gem! Waiting for my friends, I enjoyed a frisky picant0 mocktail on the roof terrace, soaking up the sunshine and the fabulous view. The manageress was very welcoming and attentive, and helpful with the wine selection. We shared a selection of starters, all nicely presented, substantial and delicious - especially the tuna crevice. For my main course I chose the Asian Summer salad - adding the pork belly as I thought a salad wouldn't be enough.In fact it was enormous - and extremely tasty! The vibe was chilled and we were able to have a good catch up over a really nice lunch in a restaurant with a 'wow' factor! All credit to the staff and chef for a great experience.

Good selection of drinks
The Montcalm hotel’s rooftop bar, good atmosphere and panoramic views of the city skyline. The seating strikes the perfect balance between comfort and style. Good selection of drinks.
Ahmed provided exceptional service throughout our visit, maintaining just the right level of attentiveness without being intrusive.

Unfortunately, I didn’t have a great experience at The Aviary. While the venue itself is stylish, the space was extremely crowded and noisy, making it hard to hear each other and enjoy the meal. The ambience felt more chaotic than relaxing.

I ordered the seafood pasta, but from the very first bite, the tomato sauce tasted unpleasantly acidic, so I had to send it back. I replaced it with the sea bass, which was a decent dish, but the wait for it was so long that my family had already finished eating by the time mine arrived — it really spoiled the flow of the lunch. They would’ve had to eat cold food if they’d waited for me, so I asked them to go ahead.

Another disappointment was the so-called “large octopus salad,” which cost £23. It came with just five small pieces of octopus, no dressing, and very little flavour — definitely not worth the price or the name.

I did raise the issues with the manager, who politely apologised and offered a dish replacement, but that had already been done. She also suggested we try the terrace for a drink — not complimentary, of course. I want to be clear that I wasn’t looking for compensation, but I would’ve appreciated a more thoughtful response, especially since these kinds of mistakes can affect a special occasion.

Overall, it felt like a place more focused on image than experience. I left disappointed and wouldn’t be in a hurry to return.

Despite having above average food, Aviary misses on the fundamentals.
We went for brunch at 12pm and were escorted to our seats by a flustered hostess who apologized for the delay as she was in her morning huddle. Well, the huddle continued as we walked by and so we heard all about their service goals for the day. 🥴
Our server was a bit odd and seemed overwhelmed, although we were her first table.
Our drinks took 10-15 minutes to be delivered although they sat at the bar for more than half that time.
The seafood platter was well made and worth the £20 supplemental fee to our brunch set menu.
The vibe was definitely “Girls Brunch” and all you can drink. We were surrounded! 😆
Not a bad restaurant.
Just not our scene.

reviews.text:
We visited JOIA Restaurant as a group of nine. The venue and customer service were excellent definitely 5/5. The food presentation was impressive, and overall the dishes looked great.

I ordered the arroz de mariscos, which I’d rate 3.5/5. I found it a little salty at first, but after squeezing the lime on it, the flavour balanced out nicely and became much more enjoyable. They also served these small potatoes that were absolutely delicious.

In my experience, JOIA is a beautiful spot with top notch service, a welcoming atmosphere and lovely food. I would visit again. ❤️

Went to this restaurant with my girlfriends on a Friday evening.
Upstairs is a rooftop bar with a great atmosphere and a wide selection of drinks.
The food and drinks are on the pricier side, but the ambiance makes up for it.
The cuisine is a fusion of Portuguese and Spanish flavors.
We ordered a variety of dishes to try — the food was flavorful and satisfying, especially for someone trying Portuguese cuisine for the first time.
The service was also very good.

Beautiful restaurant
Not much of a view if you look down because it is train tracks.
However, if you look up then it’s gorgeous specifically when the sun is setting.
Service impeccable. Attention to every single  detail.
The food was delicious too however for me a bit too oily.
The quantity served for the price is disappointing.
Unfortunately they don’t have any vegan desserts.

We celebrated our wedding anniversary at Joia, and it was a truly lovely experience. The food was amazing, with authentic Portuguese flavors and a stunning view of Battersea Park and the Power Station. We highly recommend the octopus—it's fantastic! We tried the Chef's Menu, and it was a great way to enjoy a variety of dishes. It was also a pleasure meeting Chef Rafa. We’ll definitely be coming back!

We had a lovely visit to this restaurant!
Must say that to get there it was a bit confusing due to the lifts system within the hotel. We had to find staff to allow us to get up there as we were pressing the buttons and it didn’t seem like it was working. But maybe it was just a “us” thing!
We arrived at the restaurant and we were greeted warmly by the staff and the atmosphere was brilliant. Service was flawless and the food was excellent.
Must say that I drank London Essence for the first time (White peach & jasmine flavour) and this is now my favourite drink ever!
Additionally, this was a meal out to celebrate my partner’s birthday and according to my note left on the booking form, they presented him a cake at the end with a happy birthday note. Really thoughtful gesture and the cake was brilliant. Definitely coming back.

venues.name: Pergola on the Wharf
venues.description: Contemporary, plant-filled tavern on the water offering cocktails & casual bites.

reviews.text:
Came here with some colleagues for an evening meal.
Service was good and efficient, and we all enjoyed our food.

I had the cheeseburger, which was made of 2 patties (not really smashed as per the description) which had a good taste.  Plenty of cheese and a nice soft bun.

The place is really nicely decorated and they have some amazing wraparound views with tables outside.

Another birthday celebration done! This was a last minute booking but very much worth it! We thoroughly enjoyed our time at Pergola. Loved the the vibe and will have to return to dance a little more. Thank you to our waiter for it night, unfortunately I cannot remember his name.

A lovely place to eat, food is great, with great service and a nice atmosphere.
In the middle of the iconic Canary wharf- what is not to like. We were a party of 11 after a work operations meeting and the company was enjoyable to boot, with some belly laughing.

📍 Pergola on the Wharf, Canary Wharf

After seeing Pergola all over my feed—lush interiors, rooftop vibes, and bold plates—we finally booked in for an evening visit. And yes, booking ahead is essential—this place gets busy, and for good reason.

🍽️ What we ordered:
• Korean-Glazed Flat Iron Steak with Yuzu Hollandaise & House Pickles
• Sweet Potato Fries
• Korean Pulled Beef Bao Buns with Kimchi Slaw & Gochujang Sauce
• Camden Pale Ale
• Diet Coke

🥩 The Korean-Glazed Flat Iron Steak was cooked beautifully—tender, smoky, and packed with flavour. The Yuzu Hollandaise added a citrusy zing that cut through the richness perfectly, and the house pickles brought a bright, crunchy balance. The Korean Pulled Beef Bao Buns were equally epic: pillowy-soft, filled with slow-cooked, spicy-sweet beef, creamy kimchi slaw, and a generous drizzle of gochujang sauce. And the Sweet Potato Fries? Crispy, golden, and dangerously snackable. Drinks were simple but hit the spot—Camden Pale Ale for a hoppy kick, and a Diet Coke to keep it classic.

📝 What I liked?
The evening atmosphere was vibey—think fairy lights, chilled music, and a buzzy crowd without feeling chaotic. The space is airy and beautifully designed, with greenery everywhere and waterfront views if you time it right. Food came out quick, portions were solid, and every dish delivered on flavour.

👎 What I didn’t like?
Honestly, not much. It’s definitely a spot you plan for—not ideal for walk-ins—but the payoff is worth the booking. Prices reflect the location and setting, but the quality backs it up.

✅ Would I go back?
Absolutely. I already want to try more of the menu—and the cocktails next time. It’s a perfect mix of relaxed and refined, and ideal for an after-work treat or a casual date night.

🔍 Note: First visit review—excited to return and try more soon.

venues.name: Blacklock Soho
venues.description: Atmospheric basement restaurant and bar for seared meat chops, plus cocktails from trolley carts.

address.formatted: Duke Of Argyll, 24 Great Windmill St, London

venues.vicinity: Duke Of Argyll, 24 Great Windmill St, London

reviews.text:
Better than the average.
Their steak was fantastic. Went for the butchers cut, 300g sirloin, medium rare. Sadly a few inedible chewy bits which I had to  dispose of but the seasoning and sides were incredibly well thought and became a mini buffet, taking your buds on a culinary adventure. A special shout out to the Ash roasted sweet potato. The chips were the best I've had in a steak house. Think authentic hand cut chipppy chips, but cooked in beef fat and extra crispy and incredibly pillowy soft on the inside.
The bone marrow left me a little wanting, not a huge amount of flavour for something that is otherwise normally a flavour bomb.
The salad added a much needed cut through the overall richness and doubled as a convenient palate cleanser.
The white chocolate cheesecake was incredibly rich and ended what I felt was a very good meal.
The service was very good and our waiter was incredibly positive and helpful.
Thank you for a memorable meal, this was my first time and will definitely not be my last.

The place is so popular that you need to book a table in advance. We did not; but could still have dinner there after spending 2 hours in a nearby pub. The meat was grilled to perfection and the service excellent. The waiter knew everything in the menu and his advice was excellent for choosing the food. They were out of rib eye so we went for the rump cap which was very good. And finished everything with a more than generous portion of home made cheesecake. Will definitely go back next time in London.

Blacklock Soho is my favourite spot in London. If you like all kinds of meat, go for the All In Sunday Roast (£26) – beef, lamb, and pork with all the trimmings and endless gravy. Personally, I stick to the beef medium-well and it’s perfect every time. And don’t leave without the cheesecake – easily the best I’ve ever had. Great hospitality and service, easy booking. The atmosphere is relaxed but lively, perfect for a Sunday meal with friends or family.

This restaurant is my absolute favorite place to eat in London, and we made sure to book a table three weeks in advance—it was the one place I knew I couldn’t leave the city without revisiting.

As always, the service was exceptional. John, our server, was a delight—attentive, personable, and spot-on with his recommendations, which set the tone for a memorable evening.

For starters, we ordered the cheese and pickle biscuits and the mushrooms on toast, both excellent choices to open the meal. For mains, we had the prime ribeye and a tenderloin fillet steak, accompanied by chips and roasted sweet potatoes. The steaks were flawless—juicy, tender, and cooked exactly to our request. Both cuts were packed with flavor, melt-in-your-mouth tender, and so well-prepared that they hardly needed sauce. Even so, we tried the garlic bone marrow and chopped sauce, both of which complemented the meat beautifully without overshadowing it.

The sides were well-executed, though the sweet potatoes deserve special mention. The chips were classic—crispy on the outside and fluffy inside—but not extraordinary. The roasted sweet potatoes, however, were spectacular: charred on the outside, fork-tender within, and perfectly seasoned, easily one of the best side dishes I’ve had in London.

The true star of the evening was dessert: their famous white chocolate cheesecake. Creamy, rich, and indulgent without being overwhelming, it remains my favorite dessert in London—simple yet brilliant, and the perfect way to end the meal.

For anyone seeking a steak dinner in London, you cant find any better than Blacklock. From service to execution, it delivers consistently, and for me, it’s unmatched.

We came yesterday for a dinner - and I couldn’t wait to leave a review. This place is fantastic! First of all, they only had one table at 10pm but after messaging the team on OpenTable despite them clearly being really busy they very kindly slotted us in earlier (thank you Olga!) The atmosphere is lovely, it’s not a large place but it’s buzzing and feels cosy and lively. The service was excellent - we got talked through the menu, the advice we got on what to order was great and our waiter suggested a primitivo instead of a house red which was amazingly light and one of the best reds I’ve had. We went for pigs head for starters (pulled pork on sourdough which comes with gravy), that was 10/10. We also ordered a Denver and a butcher cut Fillet with a side of broccoli salad and sweet potato. Everything was delicious! Denver reminded me of flat iron but thicker and gamier - not chewy at all and perfectly cooked. The fillet despite the size was melting on the inside with a charred exterior. Lovely sweet potato but the broccoli salad was phenomenal - it doesn’t even taste like broccoli, very crunchy and moreish with a beautiful dressing. Chop sauce is a classic peppercorn and we tried bernaise as well however in hindsight the meats didn’t need any sauces. We finished with sharing the white chocolate cheesecake and black coffees. The cheesecake was great but I’d maybe say it’s a white chocolate mouse constructed like a trifle almost with different layers you then sort of mix up - light, not too sweet, a perfect finish. And their coffee was spot on too. Our bill came to 101 for two with drinks, mains, starters, sides and a shared desert with coffee which is incredible value. All of the waiters that served us were attentive, friendly and looked like they are having fun which honestly makes such a great change from the usual. Thank you so much to the team for making our evening in London special and for the best food we’ve had in a while, we’ll be back!
